right.ask: What is the principle of moments?

explain.say: Imagine a light child and a heavy child on a seesaw in the park. Can the light one ever lift the heavy one? Yes, if they sit in the right place! The secret is called a moment, which means the turning effect of a force.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a lever. Look at the fulcrum, the load and the effort. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Balancing a seesaw with the principle of moments

explain.say: See Tunde on the left? He weighs 40 kilograms and sits 3 steps from the pivot, the middle point the seesaw turns on. His moment is weight times distance: 4 times 3 makes 12. Can you work out Mei's moment on the right?

right.label: Mei 60 kg
right.ask: What is the principle of moments?

explain.say: Mei weighs 60 kilograms but sits only 2 steps away: 6 times 2 makes 12. Both moments are 12, so the seesaw balances. This is the principle of moments: balanced when clockwise turning equals anticlockwise turning. Is the board level?

right.label: Mei 60 kg
right.ask: What is the principle of moments?

explain.say: Now Mei slides back to 3 steps. Watch the seesaw tip! Her moment is now 6 times 3, which is 18, bigger than Tunde's 12. The bigger moment wins and her side goes down. What could Tunde do to fix it?

Get a friend! Ana, 20 kilograms, joins him at 3 steps. Now his side makes 12 plus 6, which is 18, and it balances again. Brilliant work! Wow fact: a long crowbar lets you lift a heavy rock with a gentle push, using exactly this rule.

faq.a: A moment is the turning effect of a force. It equals the force times the distance from the pivot.
asks: How do you calculate a moment?

faq.q: What is the principle of moments?
faq.a: When something is balanced, the total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment about the pivot.
One side has a bigger moment, because of more weight, more distance or both, so it turns that way.
asks: Why does one side go down?

faq.q: How do you balance more than two people?
faq.a: Add up the moments on each side. When the left total equals the right total, it balances.

faq.q: Why can a light child lift a heavy one?
faq.a: By sitting further from the pivot, the light child makes a bigger moment, even with less weight.
asks: How can a small person balance a big person?

facts: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot, measured in newton metres (N m).
Levers like crowbars and spanners work by the principle of moments.

quiz.say: A 300 N child sits 2 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
quiz.show: A 300 N child sits 2 m from the pivot. What is the moment?

wrong.1: That divides; a moment is force times distance.
wrong.2: That adds; you need to multiply.

quiz.say: A 400 N child sits 3 m from the pivot. Where must a 600 N child sit to balance?
quiz.show: A 400 N child sits 3 m from the pivot. Where must a 600 N child sit to balance?

wrong.0: That gives 1800 newton metres, more than 1200.
wrong.2: That swaps the ratio the wrong way: the heavier child must sit closer.
